full_name_ar: عبد الله بن مالك الغافقي أبو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4949) gives his kunya as Abu Musa and says he settled in Egypt. His hadith on ablution and eating after major ritual impurity comes via Ibn Lahi'a from 'Abdullah ibn Sulayman from Tha'laba ibn Abi al-Kanud, recorded by al-Baghawi, al-Daraqutni, al-Bayhaqi, Ibn Mandah and others. Ibn Hajar notes some sources name Abu Musa al-Ghafiqi as Malik ibn 'Abdullah instead.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن مالك الغافقي: أبو موسى. سكن مصر.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن مالك بن المعتم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4951) says al-Tabari and al-Barudi count him among the nine men of 'Abs who came to the Prophet in delegation. Abu 'Ubayda records that he was present at al-Qadisiyya, and Ibn Mandah notes the Prophet gave him a white banner; no narrations from him are known.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن مالك: بن المعتم العبسيّ.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن مالك غير منسوب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4952) lists him without lineage and says Ibn Abi 'Asim mentioned him in al-Wuhdan through a chain via al-A'mash from 'Amr ibn Murra.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن مالك: غير منسوب.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن مالك الأرحبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4953) cites Wathima's book on the Ridda, from Ibn Ishaq, that he was a Companion. When Hamdan considered apostasy after the Prophet's death, he stood among them and gave a sermon urging them to hold to Islam; verses are attributed to him on this occasion.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن مالك الأرحبي: ذكر وثيمة في الردة أنّ له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن أبي سبقة ويقال ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4966) names him 'Abdullah ibn Abi Sabqa, also Saqba, of Bahila, listed among the Companions by al-Baghawi and others. A report via Bahili transmitters describes him seeing the Prophet standing by his camel; Ibn Mandah placed it in the Farewell Pilgrimage and called it gharib.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن أبي سبقة «١» : ويقال سقبة «٢» الباهلي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن أبي مرة بن عوف ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4968) gives him as a Qurashi of Banu 'Abd al-Dar who accepted Islam at the Conquest of Mecca and was killed at the house (Yawm al-Dar) during the siege of 'Uthman. Al-Baladhuri and al-Zubayr mention him.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن أبي مرّة: بن عوف بن السّباق بن عبد الدار القرشي
dod_s: Died at: Yawm al-Dar (siege of 'Uthman's house) — 35 AH / c. 656 CE (year of the event)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن أبي مسروح بن عمرو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4969) places him in Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr; his mother was a daughter of al-Muqawwim ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and he married into the family of al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. Al-Fakihi mentions him, and al-Zubayr reports that Safiyya bint al-'Abbas bore him a son, Muhammad.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن أبي مسروح: بن عمرو، من بني سعد بن بكر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن أبي مطرف الأزدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4976) quotes al-Bukhari that he had companionship but the chain is not sound. Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, al-Baghawi and Ibn Abi Shayba record a report in which he cited a prophetic saying to al-Hajjaj about punishing one who violates sacred limits. Al-'Askari and Abu Hatim identified him instead with 'Abdullah ibn Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن أبي مطرف الأزدي: قال البخاريّ: له صحبة، ولم يصح إسناده.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن المعتم بضم الميم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4982) gives him as al-'Absi, with the name's vocalisation from Ibn Makula. Abu 'Umar says he was a Companion who held back from 'Ali at the Battle of the Camel. Sayf ibn 'Umar reports he led the vanguard of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas from al-Qadisiyya to al-Mada'in and was sent to conquer Takrit; a history of Mosul credits him with conquering Mosul.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن المعتمّ: بضم الميم وسكون المهملة وفتح المثناة وتشديد
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن أبي معقل الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4985) states, citing al-Baghawi, that he was present at the Battle of Uhud together with his father.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن أبي معقل الأنصاري: شهد أحدا مع أبيه، قاله البغوي.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن مغنم بالمعجمة والنون ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4989) records Ibn Makula's vocalisation of the name and his statement that he had companionship and narrations. Sulayman ibn Shihab al-'Absi narrated from him reports about the Dajjal, recorded by al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Ibn al-Sakan, al-Hasan ibn Sufyan and al-Tabarani. Abu Hatim, al-'Askari and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr gave his father's name as al-Mu'tamir, and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr called him Kindi.
research_evidence: عبد الله بن مغنم: بالمعجمة، والنون، وزن جعفر، ضبطه ابن ماكولا، وقال له صحبة ورواية.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن مقرن المزني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4993) describes him as one of the Muqarrin brothers of Muzayna. Ibn Mandah says Muhammad ibn Sirin and 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr narrated from him, without citing a hadith; Sayf mentions him in al-Futuh in connection with the Ridda.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن مقرّن المزني: أحد الإخوة.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن مكمل بن عبد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4995) gives his lineage to Zuhra ibn Kilab. Al-Tabari mentioned him and 'Umar ibn Shabba counted him among the Companions, noting he had a house in Medina; he died during the caliphate of 'Uthman (no year given). His son 'Abd al-Rahman was a teacher of al-Zuhri.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن مكمل: بن عبد بن عوف بن عبد الحارث بن زهرة بن كلاب
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن المنتفق اليشكري يكنى ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4996) gives his kunya as Abu al-Muntafiq. Ahmad and al-Tabarani transmitted his account of seeking the Prophet in Mecca, Mina and 'Arafat until he met him. Ibn Hajar says Ibn Abi Hatim wrongly made him the father of al-Mughira ibn 'Abdullah al-Yashkuri.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن المنتفق اليشكري «٢» : يكنى أبا المنتفق
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن منقر القيسي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4998) says his name was 'Abd al-Harith and the Prophet renamed him 'Abdullah; Ibn Fathun reports this via Ibn al-Sakan.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن منقر القيسي: كان اسمه عبد الحارث فسمّاه النبيّ صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلّم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن منيب الأزدي ترجم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4999) says Ibn Abi Hatim gave him an entry, with his report that the Prophet recited a verse of Surat al-Rahman to them. The hadith is recorded by al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, Ibn al-Sakan and Ibn Mandah; Ibn Mandah called it gharib.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن منيب الأزدي: ترجم له ابن أبي حاتم، قال: تلا علينا النبيّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن ناشح الحضرمي الحمصي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5001) says al-Hasan ibn Sufyan listed him among the Companions, with a hadith transmitted through Sharik ibn al-Musayyab from him. Abu Nu'aym said his companionship is not established, and Ibn Abi Hatim gave the name as Nasih.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن ناشح الحضرميّ الحمصي. ذكره الحسن بن سفيان في الصحابة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن النحام ويقال بن النحماء ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5003) lists him as Abdullah ibn al-Nahham, also called Ibn al-Nahma'. Ibn Manda says he is mentioned in a hadith of Talha from his forefathers. Abu Nu'aym transmits a report via 'Ubayd ibn Adam from al-Rabi' ibn Subayh from al-Hasan in which he comes to the Prophet; another version appears in the Fawa'id of Abu 'Uthman al-Sabuni, through a chain Ibn Hajar criticizes.
research_evidence: ٥٠٠٣- عبد اللَّه بن النحّام: ويقال ابن النحماء. قال ابن مندة: له ذكر في حديث طلحة، عن آبائه.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن نضلة العدوي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5006) lists him among the emigrants to Abyssinia, as mentioned by Ibn Manda. Abu Nu'aym held that the emigrant was actually his son Ma'mar ibn Abdullah ibn Nadla; Ibn Hajar notes that both father and son may have emigrated.
research_evidence: ٥٠٠٦- عبد اللَّه بن نضلة العدوي: من مهاجرة الحبشة. ذكره ابن مندة، وساق من طريق
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن نضلة الكناني أخرج ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5007) cites Ibn Manda's report, via Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi from Sufyan al-Thawri, in which he speaks about the houses of Mecca in the time of the Prophet, Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Ibn Manda points to an error in the chain, and Ibn Hajar mentions variant chains in al-Tabarani and Ibn Majah.
research_evidence: ٥٠٠٧- عبد اللَّه بن نضلة الكناني: أخرج ابن مندة، من طريق محمد بن يوسف الفريابي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن النعمان بن بزرج ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5009) says he is mentioned by Sayf, al-Tabari and al-Waqidi. When Wabr ibn Yuhannis came to Yemen as the Prophet's envoy calling people to Islam, he stayed with Abdullah's two sisters, who accepted Islam, and then Abdullah himself became Muslim.
research_evidence: ٥٠٠٩- عبد اللَّه بن النعمان بن بزرج: بضم الموحدة والزاي وسكون الراء بعدها جيم. ذكره سيف، والطّبريّ، والواقديّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن نعيم الأنصاري أخو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5012) identifies him as the brother of 'Atika bint Nu'aym. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr (al-Isti'ab) mentions him briefly, saying only that he was a companion.
research_evidence: ٥٠١٢- عبد اللَّه بن نعيم الأنصاري «٣» : أخو عاتكة بنت نعيم.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن نعيم بن النحام ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5013) says al-Bukhari and al-Baghawi listed him among the companions, that he lived in Medina and narrated from the Prophet. A hadith through him tells of a woman passing by the Prophet and his companions. Ibn Hajar notes that Nu'aym ibn Abdullah ibn al-Nahham is treated separately.
research_evidence: ٥٠١٣- عبد اللَّه بن نعيم بن النحّام «٤» : ذكره البخاريّ والبغويّ في
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن نفيل بنون وفاء ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5014) gives him as al-Kinani, or al-Kindi. Ibn Manda listed him but said his companionship is not known; he narrates a hadith about a group of the Prophet's community that will always prevail. Ibn Abi 'Asim suggested confusion with Salama ibn Nufayl, and al-Tabari included him among the companions; Ibn Hajar notes the chain appears broken.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن نفيل: بنون وفاء مصغرا، الكناني، ويقال الكندي.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن واصل السلمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5032) places him in Banu Ghadira of Sulaym. He was present at the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq), where he brought his horse and recited poetry; the account is taken from the Nawadir of Abu 'Ali al-Hajari and the Amali of Abu 'Ali al-Qali. Ibn Hajar notes he was omitted by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr and Ibn Fathun.
research_evidence: ٥٠٣٢- عبد اللَّه بن واصل السلمي: من بني غاضرة «١» بن خفاف بن امرئ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن وائل بن عامر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5034) gives his lineage as son of 'Amir ibn Malik ibn Lawdhan al-Ansari. He was present at Uhud and the later battles, had descendants, and was brother of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa'il; Ibn Hajar cites al-'Adawi via Ibn al-Qaddah, Ibn al-Amin, Ibn Fathun and Ibn al-Athir.
research_evidence: ٥٠٣٤- عبد اللَّه بن وائل «٥» : بن عامر بن مالك بن لوذان الأنصاري.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن أبي وداعة بن صبيرة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5035) gives him as al-Qurashi al-Sahmi, whose mother was Arwa bint al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. Al-Marzubani's dictionary of poets says he became Muslim and lived long, and he composed poetry about the Ahlaf; al-Zubayr says he became Muslim and left no descendants.
research_evidence: ٥٠٣٥ ز- عبد اللَّه بن أبي وداعة بن صبيرة، بمهملة ثم موحّدة مصغرا، ابن سعيد، مصغرا، ابن سعد بن سهم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن وراح براء ثقيلة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5037) says al-Tabarani listed him among the companions and cited a report via Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, Safwan ibn 'Amr and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr from his father, describing him as having early companionship and narrating a prophecy of the Prophet about a future ruler. Abu Nu'aym transmitted it from al-Tabarani, and Abu Musa included it in his addenda.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن ورّاح: براء ثقيلة ثم حاء مهملة. ذكره الطّبرانيّ في الصحابة، وأورد له من طريق إسماعيل بن عياش، عن صفوان بن عمرو
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن وهب الأسدي بفتحتين ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5040) notes he is also called al-Usayyidi, after a clan of Banu Tamim, while one report calls him a man of Banu Asad then Banu Ghanm. He is recorded by Ibn al-Athir (Usd al-Ghaba), and poetry by him appears in Ibn Ishaq's account of the Battle of Hunayn.
research_evidence: ٥٠٤٠- عبد اللَّه بن وهب الأسدي: بفتحتين، ويقال الأسيّدي، بضم الهمزة وفتح السين وتشديد الياء، نسبة إلى بطن من بني تميم.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن ياسر بن مالك ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5046) identifies him as son of Yasir ibn Malik al-'Ansi and brother of 'Ammar ibn Yasir. Ibn al-Kalbi is quoted that Yasir, Sumayya and their son 'Ammar had companionship, with the Prophet's saying 'Patience, family of Yasir, your appointment is Paradise'. Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) says Abdullah was among the earliest to accept Islam and died in Mecca before the Hijra.
research_evidence: ٥٠٤٦- عبد اللَّه بن ياسر: بن مالك العنسيّ، بالنون. يأتي نسبه في ترجمة عمار بن ياسر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن ياميل آخره لام ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5047) notes the spelling of his name ending in lam, as he saw it carefully written in the hand of al-Sarifini. Al-'Abbas ibn 'Uqda mentioned him in his collection of the chains of the hadith 'Whoever I am his mawla, 'Ali is his mawla', citing a chain through Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father.
research_evidence: ٥٠٤٧- عبد اللَّه بن ياميل: آخره لام- رأيته مجوّدا بخط الصّريفيني.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن يزيد القارىء الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5049) notes that some scholars distinguished him from 'Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Khatmi. It cites a report in which the Prophet heard a man reciting Qur'an, was told it was 'Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Ansari, and said the recitation reminded him of a verse; Ibn Manda judged this report unusual (gharib), and other versions via Hisham ibn 'Urwa from 'A'isha (in al-Bukhari) do not name him or name 'Abbad ibn Bishr.
research_evidence: ٥٠٤٩- عبد اللَّه بن يزيد القارئ الأنصاري: فرّق بعضهم بينه وبين الخطميّ.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن يزيد الخثعمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5051) says Ibn Abi 'Asim mentioned him in al-Wuhdan (narrators with a single transmitter). He narrates a hadith similar to that of 'Abdullah ibn Hawala on the merits of the people of Syria, transmitted through several chains including Yahya ibn Abi Kathir and Abu Qilaba.
research_evidence: ٥٠٥١ ز- عبد اللَّه بن يزيد الخثعميّ: ذكره ابن أبي عاصم في الوحدان، وأخرج عن محمد بن ثابت
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله العدويكان اسمه السائب فغيره ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5062) says his name was al-Sa'ib and the Prophet changed it to Abdullah, and that he settled in Egypt, following al-Dhahabi's entry. Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) describes him as a man of Banu 'Adi whose name the Prophet changed from al-Sa'ib to Abdullah; Ibn Hajar discusses differences between these presentations.
research_evidence: ٥٠٦٢- عبد اللَّه العدوي «٦» : كان اسمه السائب، فغيّره النبيّ صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم، نزل مصر، كذا ترجم له الذهبي.
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله والد قابوس غير منسوب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5072) counts him among the people of Kufa and notes disagreement over his name. Ibn Manda transmitted via 'Ali ibn Salih ibn Hayy from Simak ibn Harb from Qabus ibn Abdullah from his father a report about Umm al-Fadl coming to the Prophet, on sprinkling for a boy's urine and washing for a girl's. Abu Nu'aym says Abu Qabus's name is given as al-Mukhariq, or Abu al-Mukhariq ibn Sulaym.
research_evidence: ٥٠٧٢- عبد اللَّه، والد قابوس: غير منسوب «١» . عداده في أهل الكوفة، مختلف في
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله جد أبي ظبيان الكوفي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5073) cites al-Khatib's report via Sa'id ibn 'Amir al-Dub'i from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan from his father from his grandfather, saying he saw the Prophet kiss al-Hasan. bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6135) lists Uwaymir al-Hudhali, also called Uwaym. Ibn Abi Khaythama, al-Haytham ibn Kulayb and al-Tabarani transmit from him, through a weak chain via his grandson Amr ibn Tamim, the report of his sister Mulayka being killed while pregnant and the Prophet's ruling of blood-money for her and a ghurra for the unborn child. He also narrates the Prophet's instruction on eating game.

full_name_ar: عروة بن عامر بن عبيد بن رفاعة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6796) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Abu Musa mentioned him, citing al-Isma'ili, via a chain of Ibn Jurayj from 'Amr ibn Dinar. Ibn Hajar says the correct chain is 'from 'Urwa ibn 'Amir, from 'Ubayd ibn Rifa'a' (والصواب: عن عروة بن عامر، عن عبيد بن رفاعة), so this is not a separate Companion.
research_evidence: عروة بن عامر بن عبيد بن رفاعة: ذكره أبو موسى، وعزاه للإسماعيلي، وقال: روى من طريق ابن جريج، عن عمرو بن دينار
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: Ata'a Mwla Abi Ahmed bin Jhsh
full: Ata'a Mwla Abi Ahmed bin Jhsh
full_name_ar: عطاء مولى أبي احمد بن جحش ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists 'Ata', client of Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh (entry 6805), in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. He narrated a hadith without naming his source, so some counted him a Companion. Citing Ibn Abi Hatim from his father, followed by al-'Askari, the page says his hadith from the Prophet is mursal (disconnected).
research_evidence: عطاء مولى أبي أحمد بن جحش. أرسل حديثا فذكره بعضهم في الصحابة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عفيف بن الحارث اليماني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6810) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Al-Tabarani listed him among the Companions and Abu Nu'aym followed. Ibn Hajar says the name is an error and is really Ghudayf (غضيف), spelled with two dotted letters.
research_evidence: عفيف بن الحارث اليماني: ذكره الطبراني في الصحابة، وتبعه أبو نعيم: فروى من طريق المعافى بن عمران، عن أبي بكر الشيباني
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عقبة بن الحارث الفهري أمير المغرب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6812) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. It calls him governor of the Maghrib for Mu'awiya and Yazid, and quotes Ibn Yunus that he is said to have companionship but this is not sound. Ibn Hajar says this is 'Uqba ibn Nafi' ibn al-Harith, named here after his grandfather.
research_evidence: عقبة بن الحارث الفهري: أمير المغرب لمعاوية ويزيد. قال ابن يونس: يقال له صحبة، ولا يصح
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عقبة بن نافع صحف بعض الرواة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists this name (entry 6816) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. He says some narrators corrupted the father's name, and the correct name is 'Uqba ibn 'Amir; the report is cited from al-Isma'ili via Ishaq al-Azraq.
research_evidence: عقبة بن نافع: صحف بعض الرواة أباه أيضا، والصواب عقبة بن عامر. روى الإسماعيلي، من طريق إسحاق الأزرق
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: Amarh bin al-Walid bin al-Mughira bin Ab
full: Amarh bin al-Walid bin al-Mughira bin Abd
full_name_ar: عمارة بن الوليد بن المغيرة بن عبد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6833) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Ibn Fathun added him, citing Muqatil's Qur'an commentary on Surat al-Muddaththir verse 11 about the sons of al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. Ibn Hajar says the sons who became Muslim were Khalid, Hisham and al-Walid, and that 'Umara died an unbeliever.
research_evidence: عمارة بن الوليد بن المغيرة بن عبد الله بن عمر بن مخزوم: استدركه ابن فتحون، وعزاه لمقاتل، فإنه قال في تفسيره
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمر بن عبيد الله بن أبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6845) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. It calls him a Successor (tabi'i) who narrated from Anas, and says some narrators wrongly placed him among the Companions; Ibn Manda said this is not sound. Ibn Hajar explains the report is actually 'Umar's account that Anas ibn Malik led them in prayer.
research_evidence: عمر بن عبيد الله بن أبي زياد: تابعي، روى عن أنس، غلط بعض الرواة فذكره في الصحابة. قال ابن مندة: لا يصح
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمر بن عوف حليف بني عامر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6846) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed. Ibn Shahin mentioned him via al-Waqidi as a Yemeni ally of Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy. Ibn Hajar says the correct name is 'Amr ibn 'Awf, with a fatha on the 'ayn.
research_evidence: عمر بن عوف حليف بني عامر بن لؤي. ذكره ابن شاهين، وروى من طريق الواقدي، قال: عمر بن عوف يماني، حليف بني عامر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن جندب الوادعي أبو عطية ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6851) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. It calls him a well-known Successor who heard from 'Ali and Ibn Mas'ud. Because he narrated a hadith directly from the Prophet without naming his source (about women at a funeral), 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-'Askari wrongly listed him among the Companions.
research_evidence: عمرو بن جندب الوادعي:، أبو عطية. تابعي مشهور، سمع عليا، وابن مسعود، وأرسل حديثا فذكره علي بن سعيد العسكري في الصحابة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن حرام الأنصاري ترجم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6853) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Al-Nasa'i gave him a heading in the Manaqib section of his book, between Salman al-Farisi and Khalid ibn al-Walid, via a report from 'Amr ibn Dinar. Ibn Hajar says the 'family of 'Amr' meant in the report is his son 'Abd Allah, father of Jabir, and Jabir himself.
research_evidence: عمرو بن حرام الأنصاري: ترجم له النسائي في كتاب المناقب، فذكره بعد سلمان الفارسي، وقبل خالد بن الوليد
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: 'Amr bin Salm bin Hsyrh bin Salm
full: 'Amr bin Salm bin Hsyrh bin Salm
full_name_ar: عمرو بن سالم بن حصيرة بن سالم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6858) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as separate Companions. It quotes Ibn al-Athir that Abu Musa added this entry to Ibn Manda's list, citing Ibn Shahin, without justification. The page explains that differing versions of his grandfather's name led them to think he was two people.
research_evidence: عمرو بن سالم بن حصيرة بن سالم الخزاعي: قال ابن الأثير: أخرج أبو موسى هذه الترجمة مستدركا على ابن مندة، وعزاه لابن شاهين
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن سعد الخير أشار اليه ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists this name (entry 6862) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Ibn al-Athir mentioned it under 'Amr ibn Sa'd, citing Abu Musa. Ibn Hajar says this arose from words dropped from a manuscript copy, and that 'al-Khayr' belongs to Abu Sa'd, so there is no such separate person.
research_evidence: عمرو بن سعد الخير: أشار إليه ابن الأثير في ترجمة عمرو بن سعد، وعزاه لأبي موسى. وقد وهم عليه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن أبي سفيان الثقفي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6866) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Ibn Manda recorded his hadith via Rawh ibn 'Ubada from his nephew 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Sufyan, on the Prophet forbidding drinking from the chipped side of a cup. Ibn Hajar treats the attribution as a chain error, with the discussion continuing on the next page (shamela.ws/book/9767/2608).
research_evidence: عمرو بن أبي سفيان الثقفي: روى حديثه روح بن عبادة، عن عبد الملك بن عبد الله بن أبي سفيان، عن عمه عمرو
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن أبي سلامة الأسلمي والد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6867) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Abu Musa mentioned him from al-Mustaghfiri, who included him because of a hadith whose chain was reported differently. Ibn Hajar says a gap in one version of the chain (نقص أوجب الوهم) caused the mistake.
research_evidence: عمرو بن أبي سلامة الأسلمي، والد أبي حدرد. ذكره أبو موسى عن المستغفري، والمستغفري ذكره من أجل حديث اختلف في سنده
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن سلمة الضمري وقع كذلك ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists this name (entry 6868) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. The name appears this way in al-Daraqutni's al-'Ilal via Haywa ibn Shurayh from Ibn al-Had. Ibn Hajar says the correct name is 'Umayr ibn Salama, as al-Darawardi and others narrated it from Ibn al-Had.
research_evidence: عمرو بن سلمة الضمري: وقع كذلك في العلل للدارقطني من طريق حيوة بن شريح، عن ابن الهاد
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن عبد الله العدوي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6874) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Ibn Fathun mentioned him from al-Umawi's Maghazi as the man who shaved the Prophet's head. Ibn Hajar says this is a copying error (وهذا خطأ نشأ عن تصحيف) and the man was really Ma'mar.
research_evidence: عمرو بن عبد الله العدوي: ذكره ابن فتحون عن الأموي في مغازيه، وأنه الذي حلق رأس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: 'Amr bin Ghnm bin Mazn bin Qays
full: 'Amr bin Ghnm bin Mazn bin Qays
full_name_ar: عمرو بن غنم بن مازن بن قيس ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6881) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Ja'far al-Mustaghfiri listed him among the Ansar who fought at Badr and among those about whom a Qur'anic verse was revealed. Ibn Hajar calls this an error that began with Ja'far (وهو وهم ابتدأ به جعفر).
research_evidence: عمرو بن غنم بن مازن بن قيس بن أبي صعصعة الخزرجي: أورده جعفر المستغفري فيمن شهد بدرا من الأنصار
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمرو بن مسلم والد يزيد بن عمرو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6884) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Ibn Shahin listed him through a report by his son Yazid ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim. Ibn Hajar says the companionship and the hadith belong only to Yazid (والصحبة والحديث إنما هما ليزيد).
research_evidence: عمرو بن مسلم: والد يزيد بن عمرو. أورده ابن شاهين. وساق من طريق يزيد بن عمرو بن مسلم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عمير بن جدعان أورده المستغفري وهو ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists him (entry 6895) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Al-Mustaghfiri included him through a chain via Hudayn ibn al-Mundhir, which Ibn Hajar calls a copying error. He says the mistake is in the words 'from 'Umayr', and the correct reading is 'Ibn 'Umayr' (والصواب ابن عمير).
research_evidence: عمير بن جدعان: أورده المستغفري، وهو خطأ نشأ عن تصحيف، فأورده المستغفري من طريق حصين بن المنذر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عنتر بنون ومثناة وزن جعفر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists 'Antar al-'Udhri (entry 6908) in Section 4, on people wrongly listed as Companions. Ibn al-Athir added him for a hadith, attributing it to Ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi. The page then cites 'Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id as correcting the name to 'Ass, spelled with two undotted letters.
research_evidence: عنتر: بنون ومثناة، وزن جعفر، هو العذري. له حديث استدركه ابن الأثير
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: Awf bin Malik al-Jshmy Wald Aby
full: Awf bin Malik al-Jshmy Wald Aby
full_name_ar: عوف بن مالك الجشمي والد أبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6912) lists him as the father of Abu al-Ahwas, mentioned by Ali ibn Sa'id al-Askari and added by Abu Musa. Ibn Hajar judges this a mistake arising from an inversion of the name, stating that the father of Abu al-Ahwas is actually named Malik ibn Nadla.
research_evidence: عوف بن مالك الجشمي والد أبي الأحوص. ذكره عليّ بن سعيد العسكريّ، واستدركه أبو موسى
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: Ghtyf bin al-Harith al-Kndy Wald Ayad
full: Ghtyf bin al-Harith al-Kndy Wald Ayad
full_name_ar: غطيف بن الحارث الكندي والد عياض ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 6929) identifies him as the father of Iyad and quotes Abu Nu'aym that he was a companion. Ibn al-Sakan and al-Tabarani transmit from him, via his grandson Mu'awiya ibn Iyad ibn Ghutayf, a hadith about flogging the wine drinker; Ibn Shahin and Ibn Abi Khaythama also report it.
research_evidence: غطيف بن الحارث الكندي والد عياض. قال أبو نعيم: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)
